gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-tai-le: Chunky, closed-in letters: Plakkaat curls its terminals almost back onto the stem, with no stroke modulation. And Noto Sans Tai Le leaves its letters open, with strokes that taper out before touching.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-tai-vie: Terminals that sweep around to nearly touch the stem give Plakkaat its sealed, heavy look against Noto Sans Tai Viet. Tall x-height and open curves in the body let the heading land hard.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-tamil: Heavy and closed, Plakkaat packs every curve and diagonal with the same stout weight as its uprights. Impact is its strength, while Noto Sans Tamil handles openness and magnified-looking text.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-tamil-s: Noto Sans Tamil Supplement draws round forms like open parentheses. Under Plakkaat's closed, heavy letters, its tall middle band makes text feel stocky and steady as it runs down the page.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-thai: Terminals nearly seal themselves against the stem in Plakkaat. Display weight is the heading's job, while Noto Sans Thai, with inflated-bead lowercase and open rounds, handles all the reading.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-ugariti: Noto Sans Ugaritic reads friendly and clean, with barely any gap between its lowercase and capitals. And against the closed, rope-thin outlines of Plakkaat, its open chalk-arc letters keep paragraphs moving smoothly.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-vai: Plakkaat is all flat, sign-painted weight, every line the same heft. Noto Sans Vai forms solid word blocks, so it can sit at a modest size without losing its footing beside that heavy heading.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-vithkuq: Noto Sans Vithkuqi leaves the throats of its round letters open and clean. Noto Sans Vithkuqi sits lightly under Plakkaat, whose curves carry the full heft of a rope's body.
